h1: Maruay Garden Hotel — Bangkok's Biggest Hotel in Kaset with Pool, Gym & 3 Restaurants Near BTS
intro: Standing tall on Phahonyothin Road in the university district of Kaset, The Maruay Garden Hotel has served Bangkok travellers for decades — 315 rooms, an outdoor pool, fitness centre, sauna, and three on-site restaurants all under one roof. The headline draw: a 5-minute walk to BTS Kasetsart University (Green Line), giving easy access to Chatuchak, Mo Chit, and the rest of Bangkok. Rooms start from approximately ฿900–1,200/night for a standard Superior.

body.html: If you're looking for the largest, most self-contained hotel in Bangkok's Kaset district, the answer is The Maruay Garden Hotel. With 315 rooms, a grand ballroom that seats over a thousand, three restaurants, an outdoor pool, gym, sauna, and free parking — all on a prominent corner of Phahonyothin Road less than a kilometre from Kasetsart University — it functions almost as a destination in itself. For business travellers, conference groups, and anyone needing a solid base in Bangkok's northern corridor, it remains in a class of its own on this stretch of road.

Standard Superior Rooms measure 30 sq.m — compact but neatly fitted with a double or twin beds, minibar, in-room safe, refrigerator, and free Wi-Fi. Guests consistently describe rooms as "clean and more spacious than expected" for the price. Step up to the Executive Deluxe or Premium Deluxe for better views; the Superior Suite (59 sq.m) and Deluxe Suite (69.57 sq.m) add a separate lounge area and make sense for longer stays or families who need the breathing room.
"Clean room, comfortable bed, staff very friendly. Easy walk to BTS — great value for the price."

Dining options go well beyond the usual coffee-shop breakfast. China Rose serves Hong Kong-style dim sum and Cantonese dishes into the evening. Allamanda Coffee Shop runs 24 hours, covering the breakfast buffet and late-night hunger alike. And the Japanese Corner provides a lighter alternative for lunch or dinner. The breakfast buffet earns qualified praise in reviews — "decent variety, not fancy, but covers both Asian and Western well" — which is the honest summary: it does the job without grandeur.

The outdoor pool is the hotel's most-praised feature. Reviews repeatedly call it large, clean, and pleasantly quiet — a surprise for a property this size. Pair it with the adjoining fitness centre and sauna, and you have a full morning wellness routine without stepping outside. The free car park (rare in this price band) seals the deal for road-trippers heading north or shuttling to Don Mueang Airport, about 15 minutes up the road.

The location on Phahonyothin Road places you neatly between Don Mueang Airport and Bangkok's downtown — roughly 15 minutes by car to Don Mueang and a 5-minute walk to BTS Kasetsart University, then five stops by rail to Chatuchak/Mo Chit. Local food around the university district is abundantly cheap: rice plates, noodle shops, and fresh-fruit stalls within a short walk, all priced for a student budget. It is not, however, close to Sukhumvit or the Chao Phraya riverside — plan on 40+ minutes by BTS if those are your targets.

Honesty matters here: this is an ageing hotel, and the wear shows. Corridor carpets look dated, some rooms carry scuff marks and tired furnishings, and a handful of reviews mention elevator outages, inconsistent hot water, and occasional pest issues. The hotel's management appears responsive to complaints, and the overall Agoda score of 8.5 from more than 5,400 reviews suggests the problems are pockets rather than systemic — but if pristine newness matters to you, search elsewhere in the neighbourhood. If you want reliable scale, a great pool, and BTS access at ฿900 a night, Maruay Garden still delivers.

highlights.title: 5-Min Walk to BTS Kasetsart
highlights.text: BTS Kasetsart University (Green Line) links to Chatuchak, Mo Chit, and central Bangkok — under 10 minutes by rail to the major interchange at Mo Chit.

highlights.title: Large Outdoor Pool + Gym + Sauna
highlights.text: One of the largest hotel pools in the Kaset area — clean, spacious, and genuinely quiet. Fitness centre and sauna are in the same building.

highlights.title: 3 Restaurants + 24-Hr Coffee Shop
highlights.text: China Rose (Hong Kong cuisine), Allamanda Coffee Shop (24-hr), and Japanese Corner mean you never have to leave the property for a decent meal.

honestSummary: The Maruay Garden Hotel delivers the most complete package in the Kaset district at this price — pool, gym, 3 restaurants, free parking, and a 5-min BTS walk for around ฿900/night. The trade-off is an ageing property where certain rooms and corridors need refreshing. Best suited to business travellers, seminar groups, and practical travellers who want a reliable northern-Bangkok base rather than a stylish boutique.
honestChecks: If new or design-forward rooms are a priority — the property shows its age in finishes and furnishings; consider newer boutique options that have opened in the Kaset neighbourhood.
If you're planning daily trips to Sukhumvit, Silom, or riverside Bangkok — add 40+ minutes each way by BTS from Kasetsart; budget that time honestly into your itinerary.
If you're visiting on a weekend when the ballroom is hosting a large event — the lobby can get busy; ask for a room away from the event floor if you need quiet.

tips.title: BTS is Your Best Friend Here
tips.body: Walk 5 minutes to BTS Kasetsart University, ride 5 stops to Mo Chit/Chatuchak, then connect to any BTS/MRT line for the rest of the city. Much cheaper and faster than ride-share during peak hours.

tips.title: Pool is Best Early Morning
tips.body: 7–9 am the pool is almost always empty — cool air, soft morning light, no crowds. Perfect for a swim before the day heats up.

tips.title: Eat Like a Student Around the Corner
tips.body: Turn left out of the hotel and you'll find cheap rice dishes, noodle shops, and fresh-fruit stalls lining the road — meals under ฿80 are the norm in this university neighbourhood.

tips.title: Easy Access to Don Mueang Airport
tips.body: Don Mueang is about 15 minutes by car on Phahonyothin Road. If you have an early-morning AirAsia or Nok Air flight, this hotel's location is genuinely hard to beat at this price.

faqTitle: FAQ — Maruay Garden Hotel, Kaset Bangkok

faq.q: Where is Maruay Garden Hotel and how do I get there by BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 1 Phahonyothin Road, Senanikhom, Chatuchak, Bangkok. Walk 5 minutes from the hotel to BTS Kasetsart University Station (Green Line). From there, 5 stops reach Mo Chit/Chatuchak where you can interchange to other lines.

faq.q: What facilities does Maruay Garden Hotel offer?
faq.a: Outdoor pool, fitness centre, sauna, 3 restaurants (China Rose, Allamanda Coffee Shop, Japanese Corner), grand ballroom, free parking, free Wi-Fi, 24-hour room service, concierge, and business centre — more comprehensive than most hotels at this price in the area.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Maruay Garden Hotel?
faq.a: Standard Superior Rooms start from approximately ฿900–1,200/night depending on season and package. Suites start from around ฿2,200. Always compare prices across Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com for the best deal.

faq.q: Is Maruay Garden Hotel good for Don Mueang Airport transit?
faq.a: Yes — Don Mueang Airport is around 15 minutes by car along Phahonyothin Road. The hotel is one of the most convenient budget-friendly options for early morning flights on low-cost carriers such as AirAsia, Nok Air, and Lion Air.

faq.q: Is Maruay Garden Hotel suitable for families?
faq.a: Families will appreciate the large rooms (Superior Suite 59 sq.m or Deluxe Suite 69 sq.m), spacious pool, and multiple dining options. The hotel is better suited to older children and adults; families with young children should be aware that the property is not a resort-style venue with dedicated kids' facilities.

quickAnswerH2: Is Maruay Garden Hotel worth it in 2025?
quickAnswerHtml: Yes — for value-focused travellers and business guests needing a northern Bangkok base. Pool, gym, 3 restaurants, free parking, and a 5-min BTS walk from ฿900/night is genuinely hard to match in the Kaset area. Just accept the trade-off: this is an ageing property, not a shiny boutique.
